### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Spec fields the frontends read must actually be produced (#99, #45)
**What happened:** article responses never include `favorited`, so every RealWorld frontend

served as `favoriteCount`, and `createdAt/updatedAt` as `created/updated`.

response against the spec's object shape, not against what our own client happens to read.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > The `?favorited=` filter compares the wrong column
**What happened:** `findAll()` collects the ids of the articles a user favourited and then
filters `article.authorId IN (:ids)` — the article ids are being compared to author ids. Even
once the `favorites` relation is loaded, the result is wrong.

**Rule:** when a filter is "articles in this set", the column is `article.id`. Read the
`andWhere` literally; do not trust the variable name.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > What it is
A backend implementing the [RealWorld](https://github.com/gothinkster/realworld) API spec
(Medium clone: users, profiles, articles, comments, tags, favourites, follows). Any RealWorld
frontend (React, Vue, Angular…) is expected to work against it unchanged — **spec conformance
is the contract**, not just "it works with our own client".

Pinned at upstream commit `c1c2cc4` of `lujakob/nestjs-realworld-example-app` (2021-01-18).

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Every handler returns the RO envelope, never a bare entity (#57)
**What happened:** `ArticleController.create()` returned `ArticleEntity` directly while every
other handler returns `{ article }`. The React frontend read `response.article.slug` → `Cannot
read property 'slug' of undefined` right after creating an article. The server logged nothing —
from its side the request succeeded.

**Rule:** the envelope (`ArticleRO`, `UserRO`, …) is the contract with every RealWorld client.
A handler whose return type is not a `*RO` interface is a bug even if it "works" in Postman.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > A relation that is not eager is `undefined`, not `[]`
**What happened:** `ArticleService.favorite()` loads the user with `findOne(id)` and then calls
`user.favorites.findIndex(...)`. `favorites` is a non-eager `@ManyToMany`, so it is `undefined`
→ `TypeError: Cannot read property 'findIndex' of undefined` → 500 on
`POST /articles/:slug/favorite`. Same pattern in `findAll()` for `?favorited=` (`author.favorites.map`).

**Rule:** before touching `entity.relation` in a service, find the `relations: [...]` or the
`eager: true` that loads it. If neither exists, the property is `undefined`.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Never `Object.assign` a request body onto a persisted entity (#112)
**What happened:** `UserService.update()` and `ArticleService.update()` both merge the raw body
into the loaded entity. Any extra field the client sends — `id`, `password`, `authorId`,
`favoriteCount` — is persisted. The DTO type is a TypeScript annotation; it strips nothing at
runtime, and `PUT /user` / `PUT /articles/:slug` have no validation pipe.

**Rule:** copy the allowed fields by name, or whitelist with a validation pipe
(`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true`). The DTO class is not a filter.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > `simple-array` is a string; `LIKE %x%` matches substrings
**What happened:** `GET /articles?tag=java` returned articles tagged `javascript`, because
`tagList` is one comma-joined column and the filter is `article.tagList LIKE '%java%'`.

**Rule:** a `simple-array` filter needs delimiter-aware matching (e.g. compare against
`,java,` on `CONCAT(',', tagList, ',')`, or `FIND_IN_SET`), or a real join table.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Static routes are declared before parameterised ones (#7)
**What happened:** `GET /articles/feed` was declared *after* `GET /articles/:slug`, so Nest
matched `feed` as a slug and the feed endpoint returned `{ article: undefined }`. Fixed by moving
`getFeed()` above `findOne()` in `ArticleController`.

**Rule:** in a controller, any literal path (`feed`, `popular`, `search`) goes above the `:slug`
handler. Order in the class is match order.

| Action | Ownership check |
|---|---|
| `PUT /articles/:slug` | none — `ArticleService.update(slug, body)` does `Object.assign(article, body)` and saves |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug` | none — `delete({slug})` |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` | none — and comments have no author to compare against anyway |
| `DELETE /users/:slug` | none, and unguarded |
| `PUT /user` | implicitly the caller (`@User('id')`), fine |

The Swagger `@ApiResponse({ status: 403 })` lines on the article controller describe an

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > DTOs
Plain classes in `dto/`, `readonly` fields. Only `CreateUserDto` carries `class-validator`

The custom `ValidationPipe` is applied **per handler** with `@UsePipes(new ValidationPipe())`

| Module | Guarded routes (401 without token) |
|---|---|
| `UserModule` | `GET /user`, `PUT /user` |
| `ArticleModule` | `GET /articles/feed` · `POST /articles` · `PUT /articles/:slug` · `DELETE /articles/:slug` · `POST /articles/:slug/comments` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` · `POST /articles/:slug/favorite` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/favorite` |
| `ProfileModule` | `profiles/:username/follow` for **all** methods (POST follow, DELETE unfollow) |

Everything else is **public**: `GET /articles`, `GET /articles/:slug`,
`GET /articles/:slug/comments`, `GET /profiles/:username`, `GET /tags`, `POST /users`,

`ArticleService.slugify()` = `slug(title, {lower: true}) + '-' + <6 base-36 chars from Math.random()>`.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > The response envelope and the `RO` suffix
`RO` means **Response Object**. Every controller method returns the RealWorld envelope, named
`<Thing>RO` in `*.interface.ts`:

| Endpoint family | Returns | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| single article | `ArticleRO` | `{ article: {...} }` |
| list | `ArticlesRO` | `{ articles: [...], articlesCount: n }` |
| comments | `CommentsRO` | `{ comments: [...] }` |
| user | `UserRO` | `{ user: {..., token} }` |
| profile | `ProfileRO` | `{ profile: {..., following} }` |

bare entity instead of the envelope breaks every RealWorld client (see `LESSONS.md`).

**Refined prompt:** Determine whether the always-empty heart icon is a backend or frontend defect in this NestJS RealWorld API, name the root cause at file:line, fix it at its single source rather than per call site, and state the blast radius and whether existing data is already wrong. · Assumptions: the frontend is a stock RealWorld client (not in this repo), so I'm diagnosing the API response contract against the spec rather than reading client code.

## Backend. The field the heart binds to is never produced.

### Root cause

`src/article/article.entity.ts:44-45` — the entity has no `favorited` property at all:

```ts
@Column({default: 0})
favoriteCount: number;
```

And every read path returns that raw entity straight to the client:

- `src/article/article.service.ts:63` — `return {articles, articlesCount};`
- `src/article/article.service.ts:98` — `return {article};`

So `article.favorited` is `undefined` on the wire → falsy → empty heart, unconditionally. `favoritesCount` is likewise served under the wrong name (`favoriteCount`, singular).

**Why it surfaces now rather than at compile time:** `src/article/article.interface.ts:7-18` *does* declare the correct shape (`favorited?: boolean`, `favoritesCount?`) — but `ArticleRO.article` is typed `ArticleEntity` (`article.interface.ts:25`), not `ArticleData`. `ArticleData` is dead code. TypeScript has never once checked the response against the spec, so the gap stayed invisible while the write path looked fine. This is exactly the failure LESSONS.md:95-102 records for #99/#45.

**Second half of the root cause:** `favorited` is per-caller, and the read path doesn't know who the caller is. `GET /articles` and `GET /articles/:slug` are not in the middleware list (`article.module.ts:23-31`), and neither handler takes `@User('id')` (`article.controller.ts:25`, `:39`). Identity has to be plumbed in before the boolean can be computed — the `@User()` decorator works on unguarded routes and returns `undefined` without a token (`user.decorator.ts:12-17`).

### Is existing data already wrong? Yes — and this fix alone won't fill the heart.

`ArticleService.favorite()` at `article.service.ts:133-135`:

```ts
const user = await this.userRepository.findOne(id);
const isNewFavorite = user.favorites.findIndex(_article => _article.id === article.id) < 0;
```

`UserEntity.favorites` is a non-eager `@ManyToMany` (`user.entity.ts:33-35`), so `findOne(id)` leaves it `undefined` and line 135 throws `TypeError: Cannot read property 'findIndex' of undefined` → **`POST /articles/:slug/favorite` currently 500s for every request**. Same defect at `unFavorite()` (`:149-151`) and at `findAll()`'s `?favorited=` branch (`:44-45`).

Which means `user_favorites_article` is almost certainly empty and `favoriteCount` was never incremented. Your client is showing an optimistic heart that dies on reload — the server never recorded the favorite. Both paths need fixing for the icon to light up.

### The fix — one mapper, one identity lookup

Add a response builder to `ArticleService`, mirroring `UserService.buildUserRO` (`user.service.ts:116`) and the way `ProfileService.findProfile()` computes `following` (`profile.service.ts:43-45`). Every return point routes through it; nothing is patched per call site.

```ts
// src/article/article.service.ts
private async favoritedIds(userId?: number): Promise<Set<number>> {
  if (!userId) return new Set();
  const user = await this.userRepository.findOne(userId, { relations: ['favorites'] });
  return new Set((user && user.favorites ? user.favorites : []).map(a => a.id));
}

private buildArticleRO(article: ArticleEntity, favorited: Set<number>): ArticleData {
  return {
    slug: article.slug,
    title: article.title,
    description: article.description,
    body: article.body,
    tagList: article.tagList,
    createdAt: article.created,        // spec name
    updatedAt: article.updated,
    favorited: favorited.has(article.id),
    favoritesCount: article.favoriteCount,   // spec name
    author: article.author,
  };
}
```

One `favoritedIds()` call per request covers a whole page of articles — no N+1.

Then three supporting changes, all at the same boundary:

1. **`article.interface.ts:25,29`** — retype the envelopes to `ArticleData` / `ArticleData[]` and make `favorited`/`favoritesCount` required. This is what makes the compiler enforce the contract from now on instead of silently accepting a bare entity.
2. **`article.controller.ts:25,39`** — add `@User('id') userId: number` to `findAll` and `findOne`, pass it through.
3. **`article.service.ts:133,149`** — add `{ relations: ['favorites'] }` to both `userRepository.findOne(id)` calls so the write path stops throwing.

### Blast radius

Every consumer of the article shape changes at once, because they all return the same envelope:

- `findAll:63`, `findFeed:93`, `findOne:98`, `favorite:144`, `unFavorite:162`, `addComment:111`, `deleteComment:124/126`, `update:194` — all must go through `buildArticleRO`.
- `create()` (`article.service.ts:170`, `controller.ts:52`) returns a bare `ArticleEntity`, not an envelope — that's LESSONS.md:49-57 (#57). Retyping `ArticleRO` will make the compiler flag it; fix it in the same pass.
- `created`→`createdAt` and `updated`→`updatedAt` rename at the response boundary only. **Do not rename the DB columns** — `synchronize: true` (schema.md:6) would attempt a schema change, and CURRENT_FOCUS.md:7-9 explicitly scopes this to the response boundary.
- `author` is currently emitted as the full `UserEntity`, password hash included, on `findAll` (it's `leftJoinAndSelect`ed at `:30`). The builder is the right place to reduce it to the spec's profile shape — flagging it, but it's a separate concern from your heart icon.
- `?favorited=` filtering stays broken after this: `article.service.ts:46` compares `article.authorId IN (:ids)` against *article* ids (LESSONS.md:86-93). Should be `article.id IN (:...ids)`. Same feature, different symptom — the "Favorited Articles" profile tab.

### How to verify

```powershell
$t = "Token <jwt>"
# 1. write path no longer 500s
curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/articles/<slug>/favorite -H "Authorization: $t"
# 2. authed read: favorited true, count 1, spec field names
curl localhost:3000/api/articles/<slug> -H "Authorization: $t"
# 3. anonymous read: favorited must be false, never undefined
curl localhost:3000/api/articles/<slug>
# 4. list endpoint carries it per-item too
curl "localhost:3000/api/articles?limit=5" -H "Authorization: $t"
# 5. unfavorite round-trips back to false / 0
curl -X DELETE localhost:3000/api/articles/<slug>/favorite -H "Authorization: $t"
```

The failing assertion today is #1 (500) and #2/#3/#4 (key absent entirely). Anonymous must return `false`, not omit the key — a stock RealWorld client binds directly to it.

Want me to apply this? It's ~40 lines across the four files, and it's the first unchecked item in CURRENT_FOCUS.md.
